question: Why does a flash at one spot first speed up, then slow down, responses to a target there?
answer: Attention jumps to the flash, then is steered away from it. Posner and Cohen found targets at a flashed spot were detected faster for roughly the first 150 milliseconds, but more slowly after about 300, when nothing had appeared there. This inhibition of return keeps a searching eye from rechecking where it just looked.
move: A quick second look at the same place is usually wasted.
source: Posner & Cohen, Attention and Performance X, 1984
reference: Posner & Cohen, Components of visual orienting, in Bouma & Bouwhuis (eds), Attention and Performance X, Erlbaum, 1984
